hook.line: SEO is dead, the future is GEO.
hook.visual: Huge black 'SEO IS DEAD' type with a skull emoji and a falling red stock line on grid paper, swapped at 1.9 s for an hourglass and 'The future is GEO'.

beats.what: Kinetic type 'SEO IS DEAD' builds letter by letter with a skull and a crashing red line
Hourglass flies in beside 'The future is GEO' as the second half of the claim lands
Flat illustration of a person on a laptop with 'People aren't searching Google anymore'
Zoom punch as the line turns to 'that changes everything'
Timeline arrow 2010 to 2025: SEO, content overload, ChatGPT logo
Cut to the creator on camera at a podcast mic, single-word captions under his chin
'Compression' screen: Google results beside a ChatGPT answer on two phones
Glowing blue square draws itself on white as an abstract 'start engineering content' visual
Back on camera for the payoff 'master GEO' with a white pill caption

why_it_works: Contrarian three-word claim is spoken at 0.0 s and typed on screen in the same frame, so sound-off and sound-on viewers get it instantly
The death claim is paired with an answer (hourglass, 'The future is GEO') within 2 s, opening a gap the rest of the video fills
Motion-graphic cutaways (timeline, laptop illustration, side-by-side phones) change the picture every few seconds while the face returns for the opinion lines
Comment-keyword CTA for a free guide trades a lead magnet for comments, which feed reach
weaknesses: Captions are a single small word (median caption height 3.9% of frame) and hard to read over busy graphics
The first 21 s have no face, so trust in the speaker builds late
CTA is cut off at the very end, so the keyword is easy to miss
Generic 'SEO is dead' framing is a widely used claim and gives no proof
for_robert: Steal the 2-second claim-then-answer opener: Fred could knock over a 'SEO IS DEAD' sign at 0 s and hold up a 'GEO' card by 2 s, with the same words spoken and on screen.
